chunks: And from that is what he also narrated: from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hashim ibn al-Muthanna, who said:

I forgot to pray the two rak'ahs for Tawaf behind the Maqam (Station of Abraham) until I reached Mina, so I returned to Mecca and prayed them, then I returned to Mina. We mentioned that to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said, 'Why did you not pray them wherever you remembered?'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ لِلطَّوَافِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer performed after Tawaf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the two rak'ahs of Tawaf until reaching Mina?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the two rak'ahs of Tawaf, prioritizing the completion of the prayer over strict location when circumstances make returning difficult. Imam al-Sadiq’s response, 'Is it not [valid] to pray them wherever you remember?', underscores the principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual obligations, distinguishing between the ideal practice and the ruling for forgetfulness. This incident is frequently cited by scholars to demonstrate that the prayer behind the Maqam is a confirmed Sunnah rather than an indispensable pillar whose omission invalidates the Tawaf itself.
